chosen_by: Claude, 2026-10-26, for Jeff to check (docs/plans/v2-tautomers-resonance.md, bar A.3)
how: Written by reading each structure against RDKit's 37 rules. Most were seen in the planning probes before this was written, so it is a review of RDKit's lists, not a blind prediction. For each compound: what the panel lists ('listed', or 'too-many' beyond 32), how many tautomers RDKit gives, and whether the drawing's stereo is lost. A test compares the generated tests/fixtures/tautomers_expected.json with this file.

compounds.name: acetone
compounds.why: the ketone and its enol

compounds.name: 2-butanone
compounds.why: the ketone and its enols toward either side (RDKit leaves the internal enol's E/Z open)

compounds.name: cyclohexanone
compounds.why: the ketone and its enol

compounds.name: acetylacetone
compounds.why: the diketone, the enol toward the CH2 (the familiar one) and toward a CH3, and two dienols

compounds.name: ethyl acetoacetate
compounds.why: the keto ester, the ketone's enols toward each side, the ester's enol (a ketene acetal) and a dienol

compounds.name: dimedone
compounds.why: as cyclohexane-1,3-dione: the dione, the enols toward C2 and toward C4, and two dienols

compounds.name: phenylpyruvic acid
compounds.why: the keto acid and its enol toward the benzylic CH2

compounds.name: phenol
compounds.why: phenol and cyclohexa-2,4-dienone; RDKit's 1,5 rule needs an aliphatic C=C, so no 2,5-dienone

compounds.name: 2-pyridone
compounds.why: 2-pyridone, 2-hydroxypyridine, and the 3H-pyridin-2-one with the H on carbon

compounds.name: acetamide
compounds.why: the amide, the imidic acid, and the enol of the amide

compounds.name: thioacetamide
compounds.why: as acetamide, with S

compounds.name: (Z)-acetaldehyde oxime
compounds.why: the oxime and nitrosoethane; the C=N's Z is lost, as the H moves through it

compounds.name: nitrosobenzene
compounds.why: no H to move: RDKit's oxime rule needs an aliphatic C with an H beside the N

compounds.name: 4-nitrosophenol
compounds.why: the nitrosophenol, the quinone monoxime, the dienone with the H on the carbon beside C=O (the phenol's keto shift) and the dienone with the H on the carbon bearing N (from the oxime, its nitroso shift)

compounds.name: N-methylethanimine
compounds.why: RDKit's imine rules need N-H or N-aryl, so no enamine for an N-alkyl imine

compounds.name: nitromethane
compounds.why: nitromethane and its aci-nitro form

compounds.name: imidazole
compounds.why: its two N-H tautomers are one compound

compounds.name: 1,2,4-triazole
compounds.why: 1H and 4H (2H is 1H again)

compounds.name: tetrazole
compounds.why: 1H and 2H

compounds.name: guanine
compounds.why: the keto-amino form and RDKit's enols, imines and N-H shifts across both rings

compounds.name: cytosine
compounds.why: amino/imino with keto/enol and the ring N-H positions

compounds.name: uracil
compounds.why: the diketo form, its enols and dienol with their ring N-H positions, and three with an H moved onto a ring carbon

compounds.name: thymine
compounds.why: as uracil, with the methyl

compounds.name: adenine
compounds.why: the 9H and 7H amino forms, imino forms, and N-H shifts

compounds.name: barbituric acid
compounds.why: the triketo form and its enols, including the aromatic trihydroxypyrimidine

compounds.name: creatinine
compounds.why: the amino and imino forms, an enol, and two with the ring aromatic

compounds.name: allopurinol
compounds.why: its keto/enol and N-H positions across the pyrazole and pyrimidine rings

compounds.name: warfarin
compounds.why: the 4-hydroxycoumarin, its 2-hydroxychromone and diketo forms, each with the side-chain ketone or one of its enols

compounds.name: histidine
compounds.why: the imidazole's two N-H forms, each with the acid, its enols and the imine; the alpha carbon's stereo is lost, as an H moves to and from it

compounds.name: testosterone
compounds.why: the enone and its dienols toward C2 and C6, with the C=C moved; its stereocentres are not where an H moves

compounds.name: aldehydo-D-glucose
compounds.why: the aldehyde, the enediols along the chain, and the 2- and 3-ketoses; every centre an H passes loses its stereo

compounds.name: curcumin
compounds.why: 51 tautomers in the planning probe: more than 32

compounds.name: ethanol
compounds.why: nothing to move

compounds.name: hydrogen cyanide
compounds.why: HCN and HNC (RDKit's isocyanide rule)

compounds.name: cyanic acid
compounds.why: cyanic and isocyanic acid

compounds.name: ketene
compounds.why: ketene and ethynol

compounds.name: thiourea dioxide
compounds.why: the sulfinic acid, its S-H form, and the C=S(=O)=O form

compounds.name: dimethyl phosphite
compounds.why: the P(=O)H phosphonate and the P-OH phosphite

compounds.name: ethynol
compounds.why: as ketene, drawn the other way

compounds.name: isocyanic acid
compounds.why: as cyanic acid, drawn the other way

compounds.name: hydrogen isocyanide
compounds.why: as hydrogen cyanide, drawn the other way

compounds.name: nitrosoethane
compounds.why: nitrosoethane and acetaldoxime

compounds.name: thiourea dioxide, drawn as RDKit's tautomer with C=S
compounds.why: as thiourea dioxide, drawn the other way

compounds.name: phenol, drawn with aromatic bonds
compounds.why: as phenol: an aromatic ring drawn as such is read as the same molecule

compounds.name: Knorr's pyrrole, drawn in the atom order of RDKit's NCI set
compounds.why: the NH pyrrole; three with the NH's H moved onto a ring carbon; two ester enols with a ring C=N; four with a methyl's H moved, giving an exocyclic C=CH2. In NCI's atom order RDKit misses one of the ring-carbon forms (9); the panel uses its canonical order
